findings.affected_surface: Private-index checkout and attribute hazard boundary
findings.claim: The planned checkout can execute configured smudge-filter helpers before the integrity pass, so a candidate-controlled .gitattributes file can trigger arbitrary local processes or network activity even though the resulting bytes are later rejected.
findings.evidence: The plan invokes checkout-index after reading the candidate tree and relies on a post-checkout object-ID comparison for filter rewrites. Git checkout applies an effective filter attribute using drivers from repository or user configuration; common examples include Git LFS. A mismatch detected afterward does not undo helper execution or its side effects.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §1.1 tree construction, §2.6 built-ins-only constraint, and §6 Attribute-driven rewrites
findings.repair: Before checkout-index, evaluate the candidate index's effective filter attribute for every path without checking out files and fail closed if any filter is set, or specify and test a configuration-isolation mechanism that provably prevents every filter driver from executing. Add a fixture with a configured sentinel smudge driver and assert that the sentinel is never invoked and no output is written.

findings.affected_surface: Symlink preservation and tree integrity verification
findings.claim: The specified checkout command does not force symlink creation, and the integrity pass can accept a symlink blob materialized as a regular file because both contain the same target bytes.
findings.evidence: The command overrides core.autocrlf and core.eol only. With core.symlinks=false, checkout-index materializes mode 120000 entries as regular files containing the link target. The described integrity pass compares hash-object output to the blob OID but does not require the lstat type to match the ls-tree mode, so this representation can pass the stated check while violating R1 and R3.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §1.1 checkout-index and integrity pass; §2 review-packet symlink assertions; frozen R1 and R3
findings.repair: Force core.symlinks=true for checkout-index, verify each checked-out entry's lstat type against its ls-tree mode before pruning, and fail closed with a named tree-integrity error when the host cannot create a real symlink. Add a fixture or invocation with core.symlinks=false to pin the behavior.

findings.affected_surface: Path representation across Git output, deny matching, filesystem access, and MANIFEST.json
findings.claim: The plan requires repository paths to be POSIX byte strings but never defines a lossless mapping from arbitrary Git path bytes into JavaScript and RFC 8259 JSON strings, leaving denial, manifest identity, and collision behavior undefined for non-UTF-8 names.
findings.evidence: Git's NUL-delimited ls-tree and name-status output can contain non-UTF-8 path bytes. MANIFEST.json requires string-valued paths and JSON.stringify hashing, while normalizeDenyList and packetPathDenied operate on patterns described as byte strings. A normal UTF-8 decode can replace distinct invalid byte sequences with the same replacement character, causing manifest collisions or incorrect deny decisions.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §1.1 deny-list grammar and MANIFEST.json definition; frozen R1
findings.repair: Define one reversible canonical encoding for raw Git path bytes and use it consistently for parsing, deny matching, filesystem Buffer paths, manifest paths, sorting, and denied_paths. Add fixtures containing invalid UTF-8 and delimiter-like bytes that prove distinct paths remain distinct and denial is fail-closed.

findings.affected_surface: Full object-ID assertions and fixture portability
findings.claim: The test plan hard-codes base_sha and candidate_sha as 40-hex even though R4 requires full OIDs and Git repositories may use SHA-256 object IDs.
findings.evidence: The manifest design correctly says full object IDs, but the detailed review-packet test explicitly asserts 40-hex. A fixture repository can inherit init.defaultObjectFormat=sha256, producing 64-hex commit IDs and failing the suite despite correct behavior; a product implementation that truncates or assumes SHA-1 could also satisfy the proposed assertion accidentally.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §1.1 MANIFEST.json definition and §2 review-packet assertion (d); frozen R4
findings.repair: Assert exact equality with the full values returned by rev-parse rather than a 40-character shape. Make fixture object format explicit for hermetic tests and add or parameterize a SHA-256 repository case so packet construction and hash preimage handling are proven object-format agnostic.
